newsitem.title: CROATIA: Foreigners hired to rebuild Dubrovnik airport.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners hired to rebuild Dubrovnik airport.

text.p: Croatia hired the Austrian arm of Mannesmann AG on Thursday for a 60-million kuna investment project to rebuild and modernise an airport near Dubrovnik on the southern Adriatic coast, local media reported.
Transport Minister Zeljko Luzavec signed a contract with Mannesmann representatives in Zagreb paving the way for the work to begin, the state radio said.
The reconstruction should be completed by the beginning of next year's tourist season.
Mannesmann heads a consortium, also comprising Siemens and Strabag, that won an international tender to modernise the airport.
It also arranged financing by means of a 10-year loan at an annual interest of five percent, which was guaranteed by the Croatian government, Croatian television said in its main news programme.
The airport is vital to Dubrovnik's tourist trade since almost 70 percent of all holiday-makers arrive in the historic resort, dubbed the "Pearl of the Adriatic," by air.

Situated some 17 km (10 miles) outside the walled mediaeval town, it was devastated during Serb attacks on Dubrovnik at the outset of the 1991 war in Croatia. Total damage was estimated at 175 million kuna.
The airport was only partly rebuilt before being reopened for traffic in 1992, with new flight control equipment financed by a World Bank loan.
